A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STEER study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original mathematical reasoning and coding experiments, entropy-estimator validation, intervention experiments, and ablations, including Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds high-sample-budget evaluation and experiments across model families and RL algorithms, including Appendix F.3.

M1.justification: v3 extends STEER to RLOO and OPO updates using their respective advantages and on-policy ratios (Appendices C.2 and F.3). The core normalized exponential token reweighting remains unchanged; the alpha sign revision repairs parameter consistency rather than introducing a different weighting strategy.

E1.justification: The six mathematical reasoning tests, three coding tests, training corpora, and datasets used for entropy diagnostics are retained. Additional model families, RL algorithms, and sampling budgets change experimental configurations rather than dataset or task coverage. Expanded corpus provenance does not establish newly added training data.

E2.justification: Figure 21 adds RLOO versus RLOO+STEER and OPO versus OPO+STEER comparisons. Table 3 retains the same eleven comparison methods; changing the stated baseline count from ten to eleven merely corrects the description.

E3.justification: v3 adds Pass@256/512/1024 evaluation on AIME24/25 and experiments using Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-v0.3, RLOO, and OPO with transferred STEER hyperparameters. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Previously reported core training budgets, decoding settings, and benchmark metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Section 6.4 and Appendix F.3 add substantial transfer analyses testing whether STEER works across model families and RL algorithms without retuning, including entropy trajectories for Llama and Mistral. Existing quadrant interventions, clipping tests, extreme-ratio experiments, mapping ablations, and hyperparameter analyses remain despite relocation.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly says coding results average three runs. v3 removes that task-specific statement and describes all main results as averages of two independent training runs. The two-run mapping-ablation statement remains. Unchanged coding scores do not establish that experiments were rerun or that the actual run count decreased.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises W-REINFORCE's average from 44.8 to 44.0 while retaining STEER's 48.6, and the text corrects margins over OPO/Clip-Cov from 2.7/3.4 to 2.2/2.9. Figures 6, 20, and 21 add high-budget and transfer results. New comparisons report RLOO averages of 45.8 versus 46.8 and OPO averages of 46.4 versus 47.5, although OPO+STEER declines on AMC23 and MATH500. Figure 4b also displays values scaled 100-fold without explaining the conversion.

T1.justification: The original GRPO theorem, assumptions, and proof are retained. Appendix C.2 adds algorithm-specific advantage formulations and a generalized estimator; its Eq. (13) contains an extra probability factor relative to Eq. (7) under the stated importance-ratio definition. v3 also changes the global-entropy rollout measure from the old to the current policy and makes the decay parameter's sign consistent with the minimum-weight formula.

C1.justification: v3 broadens the contribution from GRPO-centered analysis to a framework explicitly claimed to extend to PPO, RLOO, and OPO. The introduction adds generalization across model families and RL algorithms as a main contribution. The original four-factor analysis, STEER proposal, and math/coding effectiveness claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 corrects Quadrant III's contradictory entropy-increase explanation to entropy decrease and explains how excessive entropy can reduce informative training trajectories. It widens the claimed robust minimum-weight range from 0.6–0.8 to 0.5–0.8 using retained results. The limitations remove the explicit exclusion of entropy-stable models and add questions about agentic and long-horizon RL.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies exact corpus sizes, ArcherCodeR sources and regenerated test cases, Zeta subset selection, and the main minimum-weight setting of 0.7. Existing hardware, core implementation details, and code access remain. The new Zeta documentation is inconsistent: Appendix E.1 specifies the dpo subset, while Table 9 lists the 33 examples attributed in the prose to the eval subset.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands the literature discussion with a new general RLVR subsection and many new references covering optimization, exploration, multi-turn settings, and applications. Additional algorithm and model references support the broader positioning. The central contrast with covariance-based entropy estimation remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting. Experiments are reorganized into four subsections, the former Appendix B.2 framework becomes a separate Appendix C, and ablation and sensitivity discussions are separated. The conclusion, affiliations, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: Tables and plots are broadly restyled and rearranged, with new Figures 6, 20, and 21 and a coding-dataset table. Existing model results are split between main text and appendix, and duplicate displays are removed. Axis revisions include an unexplained scale change in Figure 4b and erroneous Accuracy labels on entropy plots in Figure 15.

improvement.justification: The new transfer and high-sampling-budget tests strengthen evidence beyond the original Qwen/GRPO setting, while corrections resolve v2's decay-parameter inconsistency and overstated performance margins. These provide a limited net improvement. The gain is constrained by the inconsistent generalized estimator, conflicting Zeta documentation, misleading plot labels/scales, and removal of the entropy-stable-model limitation.
